candidates.name: Public K-12 RNA-seq resource (PRECISE-1K + public SRA samples)
candidates.date: SRA metadata pulled 2022-01-27; PRECISE-1K paper Lamoureux et al., NAR 51:10176-10193 (2023)
candidates.verification: DIRECTLY FETCHED AND QUOTED from the repository README, not taken from a search summary
candidates.claim: 2,710 samples total = PRECISE-1K (1,035) + 1,675 high-quality publicly available samples. Repo wording: '1,675 high-quality publicly available samples', '2710-sample Public K-12 RNA-seq resource'.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: M2's measured bottleneck is the INTERSECTION of Keio conditions with PRECISE-1K expression: 11 of 28 carbon conditions, 621 of 1,035 samples on glucose, 6 of 11 usable conditions resting on <=5 samples. PRECISE-1K's documented condition space is only 4 temperatures / 9 media / 39 supplements / 76 knockouts. The 1,675 added samples come from MANY labs via SRA, so they plausibly span a wider condition space than one lab's standardized protocol — which is precisely the side that binds.
blocking_unknowns: RESOLVED 2026-09-28: the distinct-condition count WAS computable from the repo metadata and it fails the M2 requirement (see campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage). The 'key number is not stated' blocker is closed -- by measurement, not by contact.

STILL OPEN: the expression MATRIX (log_tpm) remains behind the author-contact wall, so per-condition expression depth could not be examined. This no longer matters for the verdict, since the condition annotation already fails.
Public samples span many labs => batch/protocol heterogeneity, unexamined.
candidates.code_closable_path: The underlying samples are PUBLIC SRA data and the repo ships the raw metadata TSV (Escherichia_coli_20220127.tsv). So the compendium could in principle be RE-DERIVED from SRA without contacting the authors, converting an external wall into a code wall. Cost unestimated; not attempted.
candidates.not_new_note: 2022-era resource, outside the stated 2-year window. It does NOT answer 'what is new'; it may still answer the user's actual question, 'is there anything we can use'.

evidence.label_provenance_evidence: RNA-seq expression measurements (wet-lab sequencing), plus Keio-collection growth/essentiality as the separate truth label. Expression is an instrument reading, not a tool-derived call.
evidence.label_semantics_evidence: expression level under a stated growth condition is an assay reading, not a description of where or why a sample was collected

label_screen.evidence_gaps: mode_share and n_distinct_values (the L4 degeneracy keys for G6) are NOT supplied because the per-condition distribution is exactly the unstated number above. The screen should therefore NOT return a clean pass.

campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.measured_by: direct computation over data/k12_modulome/metadata_qc_with_p1k.csv, fetched from the repo (gh CLI to locate, raw download to read) -- NO author contact needed, because the ACCESS WALL is only on log_tpm (the expression matrix), not on the metadata
campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.comparison: PRECISE-1K alone is 621/1035 = 0.60 glucose over 9 media. Public K-12 is 0.827 glucose among ANNOTATED carbon rows with 42% of rows carrying no carbon annotation at all. The expansion therefore adds mostly MORE GLUCOSE SAMPLES AND UNANNOTATED ROWS -- glucose dominance gets WORSE, not better -- so it does not widen the condition side in the way M2 requires.
campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.not_apples_to_apples: PRECISE-1K's published bottleneck was an INTERSECTION with Keio's specific 28 carbon conditions; the figure computed here is distinct carbon sources present in the compendium. The two are related but not identical quantities, so the comparison is directional, not exact. The 42%-unannotated and 82.7%-glucose figures stand on their own regardless.
campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.incidental: sucrose appears on 11 samples here, and the sibling Fitness Browser candidate carries a KNOWN bad-sucrose-stock defect on E. coli BW25113 -- any sucrose-based cross-use of the two would inherit it.

candidates.name: Fitness Browser February 2024 release (RB-TnSeq, diverse bacteria + archaea)
candidates.date: February 2024 (latest archived release found; no 2025/2026 release located)
candidates.verification: SEARCH-REPORTED, not directly fetched. Counts below are UNVERIFIED against the Figshare record itself.
candidates.claim: 7,552 genome-wide fitness experiments across 46 bacteria + 2 archaea; ships a sqlite3 database (feba.db) + per-organism per-strain fitness tables. Prior Nov-2020 release was 6,570 experiments / 42 organisms.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: The project already consumes Fitness Browser Keio data (carbon 28 / nitrogen 32 / stress 55) for ONE organism. 48 organisms x 7,552 experiments is a far larger condition-resolved fitness surface, and the plan's F2 question 4 was explicitly whether ANOTHER organism has a better-covered essentiality+expression pair than E. coli.
blocking_unknowns: Widening the FITNESS side alone does not fix M2. The bottleneck is the INTERSECTION with condition-matched EXPRESSION data; more fitness conditions help only where paired expression exists. For a non-E.-coli organism that pairing is unestablished.
Counts are search-reported and UNVERIFIED.

KNOWN DATA DEFECT, and it lands on the exact panel this project uses: the authors report problematic sucrose and D-mannitol stock solutions, such that E. coli BW25113 appeared to grow on sucrose in the original media but not with a fresh stock. Any carbon-panel work must account for this.

evidence.label_provenance_evidence: barcoded-transposon mutant abundance measured by sequencing (BarSeq) — a wet-lab fitness readout, not a genome-tool prediction
evidence.label_semantics_evidence: relative mutant fitness in a defined medium is an assay reading, not a collection context

label_screen.evidence_gaps: G6 degeneracy keys not supplied — the fitness-score distribution per experiment was not examined.

candidates.name: MaveDB / Atlas of Variant Effects Alliance corpus growth (2025 annual report)
candidates.claim: Reported growth to 800+ members / 58 countries, >7 million variant-effect measurements across 700+ genes in human and model organisms; ~2.5M variants coordinate-mapped at 98.61%, disseminated to UCSC and Ensembl VEP.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: Our forward cell is benchmarked on ProteinGym (217 assays). A 700+ gene corpus is a materially larger benchmark surface if any of it covers pathogen drug targets.
candidates.finding_is_a_NEGATIVE: No new TEM-1 / CTX-M / KPC / NDM or other beta-lactamase DMS release surfaced for 2025-2026; the only beta-lactamase entry located is the long-standing Stiffler 2015 TEM-1 study already known here. The Alliance's growth is oriented toward HUMAN CLINICAL variants (a Clinical Atlas of Variant Effects), not the pathogen targets this project's forward/inverse cell needs.
candidates.does_not_address_M3: The Alliance's headline infrastructure win is coordinate MAPPING (variant -> reference position), which does NOT address the cross-assay SCALE problem that blocks inverse dosage. Mapping where a variant is says nothing about putting two assays' effect magnitudes on one axis.
candidates.label_screen_note: deliberately NOT screened: this is recorded as a negative for the AMR-target axis, and manufacturing an evidence dict for a corpus I have not inspected per-dataset would be exactly the over-claim the screen exists to prevent.

candidates.name: Conformal Prediction Under Feedback Covariate Shift for Biomolecular Design (Fannjiang, Bates, Angelopoulos, Listgarten, Jordan)
candidates.verification: DIRECTLY FETCHED from the arXiv abstract page: title, full author list, abstract, revision dates, journal ref and DOI all confirmed verbatim
candidates.claim: Valid finite-sample confidence sets for ANY regression model under FEEDBACK covariate shift -- the setting where a trained model chooses the test-time input distribution. Abstract, verbatim: 'even when a trained model chooses the test-time input distribution'.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: This is EXACTLY the inverse cell's loop shape -- propose k edits with a model, assay k, keep the best -- and the standard conformal assumption (train/test independence) is violated by construction there. It is the on-point method for validity in a design loop.
blocking_unknowns: IT MAY NOT SOLVE OUR ACTUAL PROBLEM. Verification found that interval WIDTH / efficiency / informativeness appear NOWHERE in the abstract -- it claims coverage VALIDITY. A search summary asserted the paper reports widths in its empirical sections; that is UNVERIFIED at the paper-body level and is the only thing that would matter to us, since our measured failure is an interval that is valid and VACUOUS (informative on 0 of 6 splits).
Scope is de novo design / fitness optimisation, not variant-effect SCORING; no work was found conformalizing DMS/ProteinGym-style VEP scores.

candidates.name: The limits of distribution-free conditional predictive inference (Barber, Candes, Ramdas, Tibshirani)
candidates.locator: https://doi.org/10.1093/imaiai/iaaa017  (Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA 10(2):455-482, 2021; arXiv:1903.04684)
candidates.verification: VERIFIED via search against the published record: full author list, journal, volume, pages, year, DOI and arXiv id all resolved consistently across the OUP page, the arXiv listing and the first author's own publication list.
candidates.claim: Exact conditional coverage is IMPOSSIBLE without assumptions on the underlying distribution. The paper's actual contribution is to map the space between marginal and conditional coverage -- i.e. WHICH RELAXATIONS of conditional coverage remain achievable distribution-free.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: IT EXPLAINS A RESULT WE ALREADY MEASURED AND REFRAMES THE PATH. Our conformal attempt on the inverse cell was 'informative on 0 of 6 splits -- it brackets while proving nothing, since coverage holds even for a useless model'. That is not an implementation gap: it is the price of the guarantee class. And the paper supplies the constructive half -- the achievable relaxations -- so the next move is to PICK AN ACHIEVABLE RELAXATION (or add explicit assumptions), NOT to hunt for a better conformal method. It also names the failure mode that matters to us directly: marginal coverage can cover 99% of one subgroup while badly under-covering another, which is exactly the per-protein heterogeneity our 0.35-0.76 range describes.
blocking_unknowns: Which specific relaxation fits the inverse cell's decision ('propose k, assay k, keep best') is NOT answered by this paper and is the real design question; the paper gives the menu, not our choice.
This CLOSES a line of inquiry (better conformal method) more than it opens one. Valuable, but it narrows rather than unlocks -- do not present it as a lever.

candidates.name: Null/WT-anchored normalisation plus overlapping-variant bridging ('test-equating') as the field's practical cross-assay scale
candidates.locator: UNVERIFIED — synthesised from search summaries of the 2025 Mol Syst Biol DMS variant-scoring review (https://doi.org/10.1038/s44320-025-00137-x) and MaveDB/AVE harmonisation discussion; no primary source fetched
candidates.verification: SEARCH-REPORTED, NOT FETCHED, and partly a SYNTHESIS rather than a single source's stated method. Verify before relying on it.
candidates.claim: Independent corroboration that the scale problem is real and unsolved: 'their scale is highly dependent on experimental methods and selection assays, requiring rescaling and normalisation'. The practical approach is to anchor each assay on shared controls (synonymous/WT and nonsense/null) to a 0-1 range, then rescale across assays via overlapping variants as a bridging set.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: A null-to-WT-anchored scale would NOT be a physical unit but WOULD be a defensible shared axis ('fraction of the null-to-WT range'), which is more than the inverse cell has now. And it independently confirms our own recorded conclusion that raw calibrators cannot transfer.
blocking_unknowns: ITS FAILURE MODE IN OUR DATA IS ALREADY MEASURED: null-anchoring needs an unsaturated dynamic range, and CcdB is 79.3% tied at its assay ceiling with 8 distinct levels -- the exact degeneracy our own G6 screen excludes it for. So the bridging idea is most likely to fail on the very assay that motivated the problem.
Requires overlapping variants BETWEEN assays; whether TEM-1 and CTX-M-14 share enough is unmeasured.

candidates.name: ACMG/AMP PS3/BS3 likelihood-ratio calibration as the most defensible ABSOLUTE anchor currently available
candidates.locator: UNVERIFIED — search-reported; no primary source fetched
candidates.claim: Clinical calibration via PS3/BS3 likelihood ratios gives the most defensible absolute interpretation of a DMS score that currently exists; rank-only Spearman benchmarking (ProteinGym-style) explicitly does not solve effect-size calibration.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: It is an existence proof that an absolute, defensible scale for DMS output is achievable at all -- which our 'calibrators cannot transfer' finding might otherwise be read as denying.
blocking_unknowns: HUMAN-CLINICAL ONLY. The anchor is a clinical likelihood ratio for pathogenicity in humans; there is no analogue for a pathogen drug-resistance target, which is what the inverse cell is pointed at. So it does NOT transfer to our use case.
Converges with the F1 negative: the AVE Alliance's growth is human-clinical, so the infrastructure and the anchors are both going somewhere our cells are not.

candidates.name: Biased sampling driven by bacterial population structure confounds ML prediction of AMR (Yu, Wheeler, Barquist)
candidates.claim: Over 24,000 genomes, 5 species, 27 antibiotics, 6,740 LightGBM models, two held-out-CLADE schemes with explicit positive controls. Finding: models key on LINEAGE MARKERS, and increasing training N does NOT rescue it.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: THE STRONGEST EXTERNAL VALIDATION THIS PROJECT HAS of its own 0-for-5 de-confounded negative -- independent group, 2025, far larger scale, same conclusion, and it reproduces the 'more data does not fix a signal-vs-structure problem' note already attached to eval/regime.py. Their asymmetric precision/recall signature is a reusable DIAGNOSTIC.
blocking_unknowns: CORROBORATION, NOT A LEVER: they CALL FOR lineage-aware algorithms; they do not build one. It strengthens the closed negative rather than opening a path.
Genome/phenotype accession list not re-verified; code+results deposits are confirmed.

candidates.name: Gene copy-number features generalize better than SNPs for AMR prediction in S. aureus (Fistarol, Gervasio, Szollosi)
candidates.verification: VERIFIED (Europe PMC core record). Data-availability accessions UNVERIFIED -- full text not fetchable.
candidates.claim: 4,255 S. aureus isolates, 6 antibiotics. LINEAGE-HELD-OUT (whole clades withheld, two schemes): gene-content F1 0.875/0.904 vs SNP models collapsing to 0.557/0.638. A REPRESENTATION design, not a bigger model.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: The only in-window candidate that is a population/representation design WITH lineage-held-out evaluation and a large effect in the right direction.
blocking_unknowns: THE ADVERSARIAL OBJECTION IS STRONG AND SPECIFIC: accessory gene content is the single strongest LINEAGE signal in bacteria -- clade membership is nearly recoverable from a pan-genome presence/absence matrix -- so 'gene content generalises' may be a DIFFERENT lineage-tracking artefact rather than de-confounding.

WORSE FOR OUR PURPOSES: in S. aureus the causal determinants (mecA, blaZ) ARE accessory genes, so a gene-copy-number model may simply be RE-DERIVING A CURATED DETERMINANT CATALOGUE in feature form. The comparator is SNP models, NOT a rule-based determinant caller -- and our own measurement plus Hu et al. 2024 says the rule wins out of distribution. Until re-run with an AMRFinder/ResFinder arm and a per-clade null, it is consistent with 'curated catalogue, laundered through XGBoost'.
Species hazard: oxacillin in S. aureus is this project's own LABEL_CONFOUNDED cell (mecA is an unreliable surrogate; cefoxitin is the CLSI surrogate).

candidates.name: Cape Verde Arabidopsis thaliana multiparent doubled-haploid intercross population (Neto et al.)
candidates.verification: VERIFIED (article page). GENOTYPE/PHENOTYPE DEPOSIT NOT FOUND -- the Data Availability section names only code repos.
candidates.claim: 209 doubled-haploid lines from 8 founders (Cape Verde). Traits include FLOWERING TIME (bolting), rosette size, PSII efficiency. Mapped loci FRI K232X, FLC R3X, IRT1 G130X.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: THE CLEANEST AVAILABLE TEST OF THE PROJECT'S OWN CENTRAL CLAIM: the EXACT trait and organism of the decisive 0-for-5 negative (Arabidopsis flowering time), moved onto CONSTRUCTED variation where ancestry is randomised by design. If a supervised model reaches a real within-group r2 here while the natural-accession panel still fails, 'population design, not organism complexity' stops being an inference and becomes a PAIRED MEASUREMENT.
blocking_unknowns: N=209 from 8 founders -- far below any threshold where a learned model beats a sparse linear or catalogue baseline.

ARCHITECTURE IS THE WRONG SHAPE for the purpose: the mapped loci are large-effect NONSENSE alleles (FRI K232X, FLC R3X) that a deterministic catalogue decodes trivially, so it would reproduce the existing conclusion rather than advance it.
Founders from one archipelago -> narrow, possibly bottlenecked allele-frequency spectrum: designed but not diverse.
NO genotype/phenotype accession found -- substrate may require contacting the authors. Verify the deposit before planning work.

candidates.name: symclatron / SymGs -- clade-held-out validation at scale (Villada et al.)
candidates.locator: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-026-03213-1  (Nature Biotechnology, ahead of print Aug 2026; PMID 42675165)
candidates.claim: Over 100,000 bacterial/archaeal genomes; withholds ALL genomes of one clade, repeated at every taxonomic rank -- 11,025 clade-specific validations. The most thorough lineage-held-out protocol found in the window.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: THE PROTOCOL is the transferable asset and is worth copying wholesale for any future lineage-held-out claim here.
blocking_unknowns: THE RESULT almost certainly does not transfer: the label (symbiont vs free-living lifestyle) is CURATION/METADATA-derived -> trips G1, and it is close to SAMPLING-DEFINED -> G3. Take the evaluation design, not the finding.

candidates.name: Within-family GWAS does not ameliorate the decline in prediction accuracy across populations
candidates.locator: https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.12.12.628188  (bioRxiv, Dec 2024) -- DOI INFERRED from the bioRxiv URL path, UNVERIFIED
candidates.claim: Human polygenic indices, European-discovery to Latino-American and African-American targets, using within-sibship sumstats. HELD-OUT ANCESTRY as the primary benchmark. Reports a NULL: sibling-based de-confounding of weights does NOT fix cross-ancestry portability.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: A DIRECTLY RELEVANT WARNING: de-confounding the ESTIMATOR does not by itself buy out-of-group generalisation. That is the exact move one would reach for after the 0-for-5, and it is reported not to work.
blocking_unknowns: UNVERIFIED citation.
Human/PRS domain; transfer to microbial lineage structure is an assumption, not a result.

candidates.name: Beyond Mendel: a call to revisit the genotype-phenotype map through new experimental paradigms (Tautz et al., 24 authors)
candidates.claim: A 24-author consensus position paper arguing that the lever is experimental/population DESIGN rather than model capacity.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: NOT EVIDENCE -- recorded because it is an independent, high-profile statement of this project's own thesis, and because its author list is the set of groups most likely to release the next usable constructed panels (a watch-list, not a result).
blocking_unknowns: A POSITION PAPER. Deliberately given NO regime triple so the screen refuses to promote it: it cannot be a finding.

process_findings: AGENT-REPORTED, UNVERIFIED — route around, do not cite: CORE.ac.uk's search page is a JS shell and its API returns 429 without a key; Edinburgh ERA reportedly has a 2024-2025 indexing gap.
research-leads YouTube search returns no upload_date, so a 2-year window cannot be enforced from search results; it needs a per-video --by-id lookup.

SCREEN COVERAGE LIMIT found by using it: rejection_gates supports exactly two intended layers (L1_AMR_RS, L4_forward_continuous). A condition-resolved expression or fitness corpus fits NEITHER cleanly; both F2 candidates are filed L4 as the closer fit, and that is a real limitation of the screen for this campaign rather than a property of the candidates.

SCHEMA GAP, and it is the important one: the 10 rejection gates have NO gate for CONDITION COVERAGE, which is the actual blocker for M2. G6 measures PHENOTYPE-VALUE degeneracy (mode share / distinct values), not how many distinct growth conditions a corpus spans. So the standing screen structurally cannot adjudicate the M2 candidates' real problem, and this candidate is rejected on a CAMPAIGN-SPECIFIC criterion recorded separately rather than by mis-mapping a condition count onto G6. Do not 'fix' this by feeding condition counts into G6 -- that would silently redefine a committed gate.

THESIS COVERAGE IS A REPORTED GAP, NOT A FINDING: OATD.org returns HTTP 403 to this environment, and two targeted searches (generic + domain-restricted to Wageningen/ETH/Oxford/Edinburgh/DTU/DiVA/theses.fr/CORE) surfaced NO 2024-2026 thesis on de-confounded genomic prediction -- only journal articles. The agent's search budget (200/200) ran out before DART-Europe/CORE APIs could be tried DIRECTLY. Do NOT read this as 'no such thesis exists'; the unexplored lever is hitting those APIs rather than going through web search.
NCBI (PubMed/PMC) blocks WebFetch in this environment; bibliographic detail was verified through the Europe PMC REST API and publisher pages instead. Reusable route.

FLAGGED BUT UNVERIFIED, likely uninformative: AMR-MoEGA (arXiv 2511.12223) and the CAMDA 2025 AMR challenge write-up (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.24.678344) -- community challenges of this shape historically score on pooled/random splits, which tells us nothing on a structured population. Evaluation design unconfirmed.

SESSION WEB-SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED (200/200) at the point F1's non-DMS axes were reached. This is a SESSION-RESOURCE wall, not money and not permanent: it closes in a fresh session, or the operator can raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION. Note the compounding cost of the earlier 12-agent fan-out -- those agents consumed search budget as well as rate-limit headroom, so the fan-out is charged twice. Sequential execution is cheaper on BOTH axes.
honest_limits: PARTIAL HARVEST. 3 candidates from 3 first-party searches + 1 verification. F3 and F4 were never searched. Do not read the small candidate count as 'the literature is empty'.
Only ONE candidate (public_k12_precise1k) was verified by direct fetch. The other two are search-reported and marked UNVERIFIED.
Two of the three candidates predate the stated 2-year window, and two of the three are effectively NEGATIVES with useful detail rather than usable substrates.
